value.body: A Legal Counsel is a lawyer employed by one company rather than a law firm. Companies of many kinds hire them to keep business moving within the law. A typical day involves reviewing and negotiating contracts, answering legal questions from other teams, tracking compliance, and coordinating with outside lawyers on disputes.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: LLB (3-year after graduation, or 5-year integrated after Class 12)

items.label: Common work
items.value: Contracts, regulatory compliance, employment matters, disputes

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Word processors with track changes, contract templates, legal research databases

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most in-house roles hire lawyers with some years at a law firm or in litigation, though some companies take freshers as legal associates or trainees. Internships during the LLB and drafting experience help. Under Bar Council of India rules, a full-time salaried employee generally cannot practise in court at the same time.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Explaining legal risk in plain terms to non-lawyers
Tracking the laws and regulations that apply to the business
Managing outside counsel and case timelines

value.title: At a glance
items: Common path: legal associate → legal counsel → senior counsel → head of legal or general counsel.
Hours tend to be more regular than at a law firm or in litigation.
The work focuses on one business, so the range of matters can be narrower.
Many in-house lawyers move in after a few years at a firm.
